note: Anonymized, invented sample set for ai-automation:benchmark. No member data. Each sample is a question or free-text statement, the articles retrieval would hand the model, and the facts a correct answer must contain (any word in a group counts; every group must be hit). type 'no_answer' samples are NOT covered by the articles: the right behaviour is NO_ANSWER or an answer the validator refuses.

consumables.title: Missing low-cost consumables
consumables.body:
Low-cost supplies such as kitty litter, absorbent, paper towels, trash bags, zip ties, tape and cleaning supplies are noncritical.
- First check the station for extra stock, including other compartments and other units at the station.
- If it is still missing, call or text before coming by Station 2 so staff can check on a replacement. Do not show up unannounced.
- Staff cannot promise stock or a date.
- Mark the item Missing in the Vehicle Checkout so the record is accurate.
If the missing item stops the unit from doing its job, it is not a routine supply question. Tell the Company Officer.

batteries.title: Missing DeWalt batteries and shared tools
batteries.body:
DeWalt tool batteries fit more than one tool, including the station blower. A missing battery is often in another tool, on a charger or in another compartment.
- Check the blower, other DeWalt tools, chargers and compartments before reporting it missing.
- Other removable tool batteries, such as M18 packs, get the same check across other tools and the apparatus.
- If it is still missing, call or text before coming by Station 2 so staff can check on a replacement.
- Use only the battery and charger made for each tool. A battery that is hot, swollen or leaking: stop using it, set it aside and tell the officer.

handoff.title: Station 2 and weekend handoff
handoff.body:
Before heading to Station 2 for a replacement, call or text Support Services first and say you are coming. Staff use that message to confirm the item is on hand and get it ready, or to tell you not to come yet.
Support Services administrative staff are not on duty on Saturday and Sunday. If something can't wait until the next weekday, contact 300, the on-shift Division Chief, who has access to the supply room. If it can wait, staff pick it up on the next weekday.

station-request.title: Station requests and facilities
station-request.body:
Use a Station Request for a station repair, service visit, room asset or equipment. From Home open Station, pick the station, then Station Request.
- Choose Repair or Equipment, the room, a priority, a clear description, and a photo if it helps.
- Tick unusable if the item or area cannot be used.
- Status updates and replies show in the station's Requests tab.
- For station supplies, use the Station Inventory Form.
- Air conditioner filters that need replacing go in a Station Request.
A hazard comes first. Electrical problems, gas smells, water intrusion or structural damage: tell the Station Officer now and keep people out of the area.

bunker-gear.title: Bunker gear drop-off
bunker-gear.body:
Gear used in fire conditions, heavily soiled, exposed to chemicals or needing repair should go in for cleaning. Do not wait for visible damage.
- Do not wash it in station machines or take it home.
- Send a Bunker gear cleaning request from Message Support Services on the Home screen. Say why it needs cleaning, when it was left, your next duty date and whether you need replacement gear.
- Staff confirm where to bring it. Leaving gear somewhere is not a service request by itself.
- Do not assume a turnaround time.

loans.title: Borrowing equipment for public education
loans.body:
Equipment is lent only for fire safety and public education demonstrations by a firefighter, never for personal use.
- Ask ahead of the event. Send a Support Services message with reason Equipment, and let your officer know. Include where and when, the audience, an itemized equipment list and who is borrowing.
- No answer is not approval. Wait for a yes.
- Power tools, ladders and apparatus are never lent.
- Approved items are normally issued on your shift before the event and returned clean on your following shift.

checkout.title: Repeat issues and the next checkout
checkout.body:
The Vehicle Checkout shows how many issues are already open on that apparatus. Each one sits beside its item with its status and a timeline.
- Still record what you see today. If an item should be there and is not, mark it Missing even if it was reported before.
- Do not mark something OK because someone already reported it.
- A submitted report is not a repair. Read the status on the issue card before assuming it is fixed.
- If the checklist itself is wrong, use Report inventory correction or Report an unlisted item in that compartment.
